children: The Justice Department is investigating whether Nvidia
structured its $20B licensing deal with AI chip startup Groq to avoid antitrust scrutiny,
reported, citing people familiar with the confidential inquiry.

The investigation centers on a deal announced in December under which Nvidia acquired rights to Groq’s technology while leaving the startup as an independent company. As part of the transaction, Groq CEO Jonathan Ross and COO Sunny Madra joined Nvidia.
The arrangement has drawn criticism from US lawmakers, who have characterized it as effectively a takeover that could weaken competition in the AI-chip market.

"The Groq story is a prime example of the American system working as designed to promote innovation, reward entrepreneurs, and benefit consumers. NVIDIA is now able to offer licensed products to the entire NVIDIA ecosystem, and Groq's cloud business is now well-funded and thriving, buying NVIDIA GPUs and serving customers worldwide. The law is designed to encourage America's startup ecosystem and promote the fundamental rights of inventors and workers to pursue their dreams," an Nvidia spokesperson said.

Regulatory questioning into the Nvidia-Groq transaction began earlier this year as part of the Justice Department’s broader antitrust investigation, the people said. The licensing-deal probe, first reported by The New York Times, could ultimately end without enforcement action.
Groq did not submit the deal for antitrust review.

title: Nvidia faces DOJ probe over $20B Groq licensing deal: report
